kurz: What repeats itself in every crisis, what turns out differently each time, and which rules you should put in writing before a crisis.

bloecke.md:
Four hundred years of financial history cannot be learned by heart. What remains are a few mechanisms that recur and very many more details that never repeat themselves. Investors who treat the mechanisms as a forecast sell as early as 1996, for example, and then wait until 2013. Those who, by contrast, mistake the details for mechanisms pay attention to superficial features such as the tulips and overlook the credit.

A useful approach is to divide things into three groups: what reliably repeats itself, what turns out differently each time and what only becomes apparent in hindsight. The third group is the most dangerous. Its insights seem compelling after the fact, but are of no use for any decision.

bloecke.titel: Six crisis patterns with evidence and consequence

bloecke.md:
## Debt financing and the timing of sales

The cases differ in almost everything except financing. At the start of 1998, LTCM had equity of $4.7 billion and around $124.5 billion of debt, that is, leverage of over 25 to 1. After the Russian default in August 1998, the fund lost $4.6 billion in less than four months.

In none of these cases did the mistake lie primarily in the assessment of the market. With many of its positions, LTCM was even proved right in the end. The mistake was that the investor could no longer decide the time of sale, because the loan agreement dictated it.
Without credit, the investor decides when to sell. With credit, a falling price can force them to sell.

## Narrative and valuation

The phrase “this time is different” is regarded as one of the most expensive in financial history, and Reinhart and Rogoff made it the title of their book on financial crises. The reason it is expensive is not that it is always wrong. Tulip bulbs were scarce, the internet changed the world, and Japan was one of the three largest exporting nations in the world. The stories were true in each case. What was wrong was the price they were supposed to justify. The price-to-earnings ratio of the Nasdaq was about 200 at the end of 1999, more than twice the Japanese bubble peak of 80.

That is why the obvious test fails, namely recognising a bubble by the fact that the idea behind it is nonsensical. Moreover, whether quality prevails can only ever be said in hindsight. In October 1929, Irving Fisher spoke of a “permanently high plateau”.

bloecke.titel: Declines progressing to the next stage (S&P 500 since 1928)
bloecke.unter: A decline of 15% turns into a bear market in almost three out of four cases; the deeper the decline already is, the less often it goes any further down.

bloecke.md:
## Missing buyers as the trigger

On 5 February 1637, tulip bulbs fetched around 90,000 guilders at the Alkmaar orphanage auction. An annual income at the time averaged about 150 guilders. Two days earlier, at an auction in Haarlem, no buyer could be found for a single bulb. The slump was not preceded by any new piece of news, a failed harvest or a decree.

In modern markets, this process is amplified further. Investors who have invested on credit or through derivatives then base their sales on what can be sold and not on their own assessment. They first sell what is easy to sell, regardless of whether it is overpriced. That is why even solid positions fall in panics, and diversification within an asset class fails at the very moment it is needed.

“This is safe.” In 2023, Silicon Valley Bank failed because of US Treasury bonds, which are regarded as the securities with the lowest default risk in the world. At the end of 2022, it had over $15 billion in unrealised price losses on its books, and the bank had to sell.

“The order of loss absorption protects me.” At Credit Suisse, AT1 bonds worth CHF 16 billion were written off completely in March 2023, while the shareholders still received CHF 3 billion.

“The government will come to the rescue.” In 2008, Bear Stearns and AIG were rescued; Lehman Brothers, on 15 September, was not.

## Different depths and durations

It is widely assumed that the recovery after a deeper crash takes longer. The data support this only weakly. The coronavirus crash of 2020 brought a drop of 33.9% in 33 calendar days and was made up after just under six months. The shallower interest rate and inflation shock of 2022 brought a drop of 25.4%, and the recovery took just over 24 months. After the peak of March 2000, around 86 months passed until the next record, and after the peak of 2007 around 66 months. The Nikkei 225 took from 29 December 1989 until 22 February 2024, that is, 34 years and 2 months.

The duration depends more on policy after the slump than on the trigger. From 1929 to 1933, the Fed allowed the money supply to shrink by about 30%, and a third of all US banks disappeared. In 2020, the same central bank cut its key interest rate to a range of 0 to 0.25% within a few days.

bloecke.titel: Depth and recovery time of 25 declines in the S&P 500 since 1950
bloecke.unter: The points are widely scattered; in 2020 the decline was deeper than in 2022, but the recovery was around four times as fast, so the recovery time cannot be derived from the depth.

bloecke.erklaerung: The gain needed to make up a loss is always larger in percentage terms than the loss, and the gap grows ever faster. That is why limiting losses is mathematically worth more than maximising gains. For the same reason, position size is a more important decision than the timing of entry.

bloecke.md:
## Position in the market cycle

If forecasts do not work and the patterns give warning signals too early, a more modest task remains, namely to establish where the market stands in the cycle. Two approaches have endured for this, and neither of them names a date.

André Kostolany drew the cycle as an egg with six phases. He reads the phases from trading volume and the number of shareholders, not from the price. His distinction between “shaky” hands (debt-financed, impatient) and “strong” hands (self-financed, patient) explains what happens at the upper turning point. At the peak, the securities are held by the investors who have to sell.

bloecke.titel: Kostolany's egg with six phases and two signals
bloecke.unter: Volume and the number of holders serve as signals instead of the price; buying takes place in A1 and B3, selling in A3 and B1.

knoten.notiz: High volume, number of holders rises sharply. The shaky hands buy back in. Selling phase.
Rising volume, number of holders unchanged. Prices follow earnings. Hold.
Low volume, number of holders falls. Securities pass into strong hands. Buying phase.
Prices fall on low volume, number of holders keeps rising. Do not buy more.
Rising volume, falling prices, number of holders unchanged. Wait.
Very high volume, number of holders falls sharply, capitulation. Buying phase.

bloecke.md:
The model has two limits. It names no points in time, and a phase can last months or years. In addition, its main signal is harder to read today than in 1960, because volume arises mainly from market making, derivatives trading and index adjustments and not from changes of opinion.

Howard Marks turned this into a checklist in *Mastering the Market Cycle* that measures the same thing, but using observable credit conditions instead of quantities. According to Marks, nobody knows where the market is going, but it is possible to describe where it stands. The position in the cycle shifts probabilities; it does not set dates.

bloecke.md:
This assessment describes the situation and is not a forecast; the picture is mixed.

- Money is becoming more expensive again. Since 16 September 2026, after two rises this year, the ECB deposit facility rate has stood at 2.50%, and since 17 September 2026 the Fed's target range has been 3.75% to 4.00%, after the first rise since 2023.
- Long-term interest rates have risen, for ten-year Bunds to around 3.5% in mid-September (highest level since 2011), and for ten-year US Treasuries to 5.01% on 16 September 2026 (highest level since 2007).
- Asset prices, on the other hand, are close to their records. The S&P 500 had last set a record close of 7,798.99 points on 13 August 2026, and the DAX an intraday record high of 26,618.74 points on 28 August 2026. The largest decline of the current year was 9.1% and stayed below the correction threshold.

The first two points indicate a cold market, the third a hot one, and such a mixed picture is the norm. A clear-cut finding is rare and even then would not dictate a point in time.

## Rules for a crisis

The eleven crisis lessons do not provide an indicator. Their result is a written plan drawn up in calm times. In a panic, the information available and your judgement are worse and the time pressure is greater. Every decision that can be made in advance should therefore be made in advance.

schritte.text: The buffer is sized so that in no scenario do you have to sell from the portfolio. Anyone who does not have to sell can wait in a crisis; in such phases, that is the most important advantage.

schritte.titel: No securities-backed loan in the core portfolio
schritte.text: With debt financing, the lender decides when to sell, no longer the investor. Investors who use credit nonetheless should work out their leverage limit for a decline of 50%, not just for 15%.

One possible rule is to rebalance as soon as the equity allocation deviates from its target by more than five percentage points, at most twice a year. The rule ensures that shares are bought after sharp price falls.
Around 76% of the best trading days fell in bear markets or in the first two months after them. A saver who suspends the plan misses these days.
The only tax benefit of a crash is realised losses that can be offset. For this step there is a method of calculation and a fixed deadline, unlike for exiting and re-entering the market.

bloecke.md:
An individual share was bought for €20,000 and, after a fall in price, is now worth only €12,000. Selling it realises a loss of €8,000. The loss is recorded in the **share loss pot** (Aktienverlusttopf) and, under Section 20(6) sentence 4 EStG (Income Tax Act), may only be offset against gains from share sales, not against dividends, interest or fund gains.

If there are €8,000 of share gains in the same year, the tax saving is €8,000 × 26.375% = €2,110, made up of flat-rate withholding tax (Abgeltungsteuer) plus solidarity surcharge, without church tax. If the same shares are bought back, the market position remains in place. In its judgment of 25 August 2009 (IX R 60/07), the Federal Fiscal Court (BFH) did not regard the prompt repurchase as an abuse of legal structuring (Gestaltungsmissbrauch) under Section 42 AO (Fiscal Code).

The approach has a limit. If no share gains arise later, the loss carryforward is worthless, while the spread and fees are incurred immediately. In any case, the share loss pot does not apply to units of equity ETFs. Their losses are recorded in the general loss offset pot.

bloecke.titel: Four rules on tax and securities accounts
bloecke.md:
- If losses are held at broker A and gains at broker B, they are not offset automatically. This requires a **loss certificate** (Verlustbescheinigung) from broker A, which under Section 43a(3) sentence 5 EStG must be applied for by 15 December. Without an application, the loss at broker A is merely carried forward.
- Under Section 18(1) InvStG (Investment Tax Act), the advance lump sum (Vorabpauschale) is capped at the increase in value of the fund unit in the calendar year. In a year with a falling fund price, no advance lump sum therefore arises.
- The saver's allowance (Sparer-Pauschbetrag) of €1,000, or €2,000 for joint assessment (Section 20(9) EStG), lapses without replacement in a year without income and cannot be carried over to other years.
- Deposit protection and the protection of securities accounts follow different rules. Under Section 8 EinSiG (Deposit Guarantee Act), balances are protected up to €100,000 per customer and institution. Securities remain the customer's property and are separated from the insolvency estate if the bank becomes insolvent.

In hindsight, every bubble seems obvious, and almost everyone is convinced they would have sold in 1999 or 2007. But only what was put in writing before the event can be verified. Your own portfolio transactions from April 2025 give an insight into how you will behave in the next crash. At that time, the S&P 500 lost 18.9% in seven weeks and stood at an all-time high three months later.
The patterns help you sit out declines; they are of no use for forecasts. The result of this module is a position size that can still be held even after a decline of 50%, and not a decision to sell.

mitnehmen: The recurring mechanisms are credit, missing buyers, simultaneous selling and maturity mismatch, while triggers, depth and duration never repeat themselves.
The story behind a bubble is almost always true, and it is the price that is wrong; a plausible argument is no substitute for a valuation.
The duration of the recovery cannot be derived from the depth of a decline; in 2020 the slump was deeper than in 2022 and was made up around four times faster.
Kostolany's egg and Marks's cycle checklist describe the position in the cycle and shift probabilities, but name no points in time.
Crisis rules are set in calm times: liquidity reserve, no leverage, rebalancing threshold, a savings plan that keeps running and a tax-driven action instead of an emotional one.

begriffe.text: Cycle model in six phases (A1 to A3 upwards, B1 to B3 downwards) that uses trading volume and the number of holders as signals, not the price. Buying takes place in A1 and B3, selling in A3 and B1.

Kostolany's classification of investors. Shaky hands are debt-financed, driven by opinions and impatient, and have to sell during declines. Strong hands are financed with their own money and can wait.

Separately maintained loss offset pot at the bank for losses from the sale of individual shares. Under Section 20(6) sentence 4 EStG, these losses can only be offset against gains from share sales, not against interest, dividends or fund gains.

Certificate of losses in a securities account that have not been offset. It is issued on application, which under Section 43a(3) sentence 5 EStG must be submitted by 15 December of the year, and it allows the losses to be offset across securities accounts in the tax return.
